### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4de4a45dc38105cac2f5a70ac44c0c36649e724b` — the merge of head `241a137fd1e3a8f7caf4b530a0e4752b232d8bf3` into base `3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4de4a45dc38105cac2f5a70ac44c0c36649e724b && git checkout 4de4a45dc38105cac2f5a70ac44c0c36649e724b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2 241a137fd1e3a8f7caf4b530a0e4752b232d8bf3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2 && git merge --no-ff 241a137fd1e3a8f7caf4b530a0e4752b232d8bf3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3482f3d8d2c48ec8d2e3306f1ce26c0364e800c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

### ① Derived judgments

- `BusinessUnitGraphService.expandUnitMembers` / `expandUsers`: a failed or cursor-dishonoured `sys_business_unit_member` read now throws via `readMembershipToCompletion`, nothing cached — RIGHT. Every caller read: `expandRecipient` → `evaluateResolvedRule` (boot-loop and hook-rebind catches), `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` (bu-tree-recompute L299, queue-hooks L218 per-rule catches), `ruleReachesUser` → `reconcileRuleForUser` (per-user catch), `OwnershipQueueService.expandSpec` (`.catch` → warnOnce, `[]`, its declared posture; `specsReachUser` default arm routes through it). No caller that must stay non-throwing now throws; the per-user recompute stops revoking a holder on an outage. Same surface the team read has had since #29602.
- Absence (`isObjectAbsentError` attributed to the object) still answers `[]` — RIGHT; every other error stays loud.
- Backfill: failed/incomplete scan → write nothing, warn with consequence, `{0,0}` — RIGHT (the boot catch would misreport "not started"); absent object → silent `[]` — RIGHT. The walk reads the member table while writing `sys_user`, so it is not self-mutating; ordering sound.
- Approvals `expandBusinessUnitUsers` → `readHoldersToCompletion`: the throw lands in `resolveApproverSpec`'s directory catch → literal + `could not be expanded` with error — RIGHT. `resolveAs` catch warns through shared `warnExpansionFailed`; `VALIDATION_FAILED` still rethrown — RIGHT.
- Public surface: no export added or removed; `readMembershipToCompletion` stays package-internal. The only accept-set change is empty → refusal on a failed member read, as declared.

### ② Semver level

Matches: `patch` + `!` + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + adr-0087 not-required, the shape of #29362; #29503 said `yes` only for its new export, which this PR has none of. Check-runs at read time: Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 2/8 and 7/8, Type Check workspace/source/consumer/debt, all Lint families, Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI = success; Test Core 1,3,4,5,6,8/8 still in_progress; nothing failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- OQ1 (`APPROVER_INDEX_CAP` drops an administrator on row 10,001, loudly): the card's item-2 rule is explicit — a declared bound with a loud warning is reported and left. Option A stands; a card for C is the seat's call. Not a blocker.
- OQ2 (`Fixes #29606` with item 2's queue half unfixed): QUEUE_READ_LIMIT measurably drops holders silently, the arm the card said to treat; the dispatch froze the file for #29604. Escalated: before merge the seat writes the measured reading onto #29604 as a comment (not only this report's JSON) or files the blocked card (B); A is acceptable only with that comment.
- Dev out-of-scope finding 1 (carrier none): a failed `sys_business_unit` read still answers nobody and is CACHED for the pass — `seedIsUsable` catch → `[]` cached in `unitMembers`/`descendants`, `descendants` child read catch → `[]` (limit 1000), approvals `businessUnitIsLive` and descent catches → `[]`. The revoke-every-member outage the changeset closes for the member table is still reachable through the unit table. Not this card's item 1 (it names the member table) and the changeset wording is honest, but it needs a carrier filed by the seat.
- Finding 3 (delegated-admin gate, fail-closed): agree, noted only.
- Skills-docs: approvals.mdx updated; no skill or doc on head claims a bound or an empty answer for these reads.

### ④ Design judgment

- business-unit-graph.ts: `readMembers` uses the shared walk; the `$and` cursor merge composes with `memberScope`'s `$in` + `organization_id`; cache set only after a complete read. Holds. The seed check before it is the unit-table gap above — should-fix, follow-up card.
- primary-bu-projection.ts: `walk.truncated` is checked after the loop with no `max`, so only a no-id or repeated-cursor page trips it; that page is yielded but discarded, so no half projection. Holds. The `limit: 1` probes are unchanged — correct.
- approval-service.ts: holders deduped across pages; the `expression` loop warns once per failed key, same noise profile as the static types. Holds.
- team-graph.ts: comment only.
- Tests: real SqlDriver with row ids scrambled against user ids, so a walk in user order would fail the 10,001 pins; 9,999 single-read controls; not-cached pin keyed to the member object; absence pinned as unregistered and as dropped table; backfill no-id truncation pin. The graph double now models `$and`/`$gt`/orderBy/limit and stamps ids, so its 25 cases exercise the walk. The queue posture on a failed BU read is asserted nowhere — acceptable, the file is frozen and the posture pre-exists.
- No must-fix. Should-fix: file the unit-table carrier; land the #29604 comment before the card closes.
